title: Likes and preferences
function: Express what you like and dislike

sections.heading: Expressing likes and dislikes
sections.body: In English we use verbs like 'like', 'love', 'enjoy', 'hate' and 'don't mind' to express preferences. These verbs can be followed by a noun or a gerund (-ing form).

sections.heading: Like + infinitive or gerund
sections.body: After 'like', 'love' and 'hate' you can use either the -ing form or 'to + verb' with almost the same meaning.
list: I like reading. = I like to read.
She loves dancing. = She loves to dance.
He hates waiting. = He hates to wait.

sections.heading: Would like
sections.body: 'Would like' is more polite and means 'want'. It is followed by a noun or 'to + verb'. It is NOT followed by -ing.
table: I would like a coffee, please.
I would like to go to the cinema.
I would like you to help me.

sections.heading: Short answers
list: Do you like pizza? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Would you like some tea? Yes, please. / No, thank you.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'I like read'. Say 'I like reading' or 'I like to read'.
Do not use -ing after 'would like': 'I would like going' is wrong. Say 'I would like to go'.
Do not say 'I am agree'. Say 'I agree'.

list.definition: She likes pasta with tomato sauce.
I love coffee in the morning.
I would like a glass of water.
She loves singing in the shower.
I like watching films at the weekend.
I would like a table for two, please.
Can I have the menu, please?
Could we have the bill, please?

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: I would like a coffee, please.
Would you like to come with us?
I don't like getting up early.
questions: In sentences 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7, what form of the verb comes after like/love/hate/enjoy/mind?
In sentence 4, what comes after 'would like'?
In sentence 5, what form of the verb comes after 'would like'?
In sentence 8, how do we make the negative?
What is the difference between 'I like coffee' and 'I would like a coffee'?

questions.explanation: After love/like/hate we usually use the -ing form.

questions.prompt: I ___ like a glass of water, please.
questions.explanation: 'Would like' is the polite form to ask for something.

questions.prompt: Would you like ___ to the cinema?
He doesn't mind ___ for the bus.
We enjoy ___ films at the weekend.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 sentences about things you love, like, don't mind, dislike and hate.
Write a short paragraph (5 sentences) about your favourite food and drink. Use 'like', 'love' and 'would like'.
Imagine you are in a restaurant. Write a short dialogue using 'would like', 'can I have' and 'the bill'.

questions.explanation: With 'I' we use the base form 'love'.

questions.prompt: I ___ like a cup of tea, please.

questions.explanation: After 'doesn't' we use the base form 'like'.

questions.prompt: She ___ to go shopping this afternoon.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Like / love / enjoy / hate / don't mind + verb-ing.
Would like + noun or 'to + verb' (NOT -ing).
Negative: don't / doesn't + like.
Questions: Do / Does + subject + like...?

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'I like read'. Say 'I like reading'.
Do not use -ing after 'would like'. Say 'I would like to go'.
Do not say 'I am agree'. Say 'I agree'.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: I love...
I like...
I don't mind...
I hate...
I would like...
Would you like...?
Yes, please. / No, thank you.
